Done. **I have not committed** — your standing rule is that you handle all check-in steps yourself, so I stopped at "diff is ready" despite `/implement` saying to commit.

## Code review results

**Spec axis — 2 real defects, both fixed and verified in the shipped bundle:**

1. **The slide-in could never appear if the reader already loaded past 50%** — an anchor deep-link, back-navigation with scroll restoration, or a short article fires no `scroll` event, so the trigger never ran. Now checks once on load as well.
2. **Dismissing the slide-in left it partly on screen.** It only re-applied `translate-y-full`, but the panel sits at `sm:bottom-6`, so translating down by its own height left a 24px band of card and the top of the close button visible on desktop, permanently — and in the tab order either way. Now adds `hidden` on `transitionend`.

**Standards axis — 3 real, fixed:** `CONTEXT.md` used "attention surface" in its own body while listing it under `_Avoid_`; the new `UTMMedium` union carried a dead `'popup'` member (the modal that emitted it is gone — the *reader* in `newsletter-tags.ts` still handles it, since old links are in the wild); and two em dashes in my own comments.

**Also cleaned up:** duplicated storage-availability functions collapsed to one helper; `STICKY_BAR_CONFIG` deleted (it held one string identical to the slide-in's) in favour of a shared `CTA_DISMISS_LABEL`; the hardcoded `aria-label="Quiz invitation"` moved into `cta.ts` and made campaign-neutral; `learn-resources-page` added to `Attribution` — it was already being passed by `learn/index.mdx` and no tool could see it, because MDX isn't type-checked.

**Deliberately not fixed:** the variant-block duplication inside each component and the 4-line variant-selection script are the repo's existing pattern (`cta-banner.astro` does the same) — extracting a module for four lines works against the simplicity you asked for. `showForm?: boolean` still violates the no-booleans rule but is pre-existing and belongs to the banner. `clearCtaSuppression()` has no caller on purpose: it's there for your manual testing.

The spec reviewer flagged `CONTEXT.md` as scope creep. It isn't — `/grill-with-docs` runs `/domain-modeling`, which is what produced it.

## Gates

`astro check` 0/0/0, `lint:tw` clean, production build succeeds. I verified surface placement against the built HTML across 15 page types — every one matches the spec, no page has both.

**Unverified: how it looks.** I haven't seen either surface rendered. Worth checking on a phone in particular: the sticky bar overlays the last ~56px of every page until dismissed, which you wanted to eyeball before deciding on the `padding-bottom` fix. The four sticky-bar/slide-in strings in `cta.ts` are marked as first drafts for you to rewrite.

/**
 * Shared constants for Call-to-Action (CTA) components
 * Centralized marketing copy, URLs, and configuration for the four CTA
 * surfaces: the two pinned ones (sticky bar, slide-in) and the two in-flow
 * ones (cta-banner, link-sidebar). See CONTEXT.md for the vocabulary.
 */

import BannerImage from '@/assets/images/global/ai-feature-factory-with-opacity.png';
import SidebarImage from '@/content/blog/using-genai-to-code-not-so-fast/images/ai-promise-vs-reality.jpg';
import type { ImageMetadata } from 'astro';

/**
 * Master switch to enable/disable A/B testing
 * When false, always shows primary content (no variant selection)
 */
export const AB_TEST_ENABLED = false;

/**
 * Variant IDs for PostHog tracking
 */
export const CTA_VARIANT_IDS = {
  primary: 'cta-sm-role-ai-quiz',
  /** Placeholder for the next test; unused while CTA_VARIANT is null. */
  variant: 'cta-variant-b',
} as const;

export type CTAVariantId =
  (typeof CTA_VARIANT_IDS)[keyof typeof CTA_VARIANT_IDS];

/**
 * Content structure for CTA variants
 */
interface CTAContent {
  heading: string;
  subHeading: string;
  /** Sidebar body copy: read at browsing pace, so longer than subHeading. */
  sidebarBody: string;
  /** Sidebar link label: plain and descriptive, not a command. */
  sidebarButtonText: string;
  /**
   * Sticky bar copy. One line, on screen at every scroll position, so it has
   * to survive a 375px viewport without wrapping to three lines. Shortest of
   * every register here.
   */
  stickyBarText: string;
  stickyBarButtonText: string;
  /**
   * Slide-in copy. Posed as a question with two answers, both of which land on
   * the quiz cover. The answers carry no meaning to the quiz (see HISTORY.md
   * on the shelved prefill); they differ only by utm_content, so the numbers
   * say which framing pulled people in.
   */
  slideInHeading: string;
  slideInBody: string;
  slideInButtonPrimaryText: string;
  slideInButtonSecondaryText: string;
  bodyText: string;
  buttonText: string;
  buttonLink: string;
  /** When true, render a newsletter signup form instead of a link button */
  showForm?: boolean;
}

/**
 * Primary (control) variant content
 * "Which parts of the Scrum Master job still need a person?": links to the
 * self-hosted quiz at /quiz/scrum-master-ai/. The hook is the reader's own
 * job, not the industry's failure statistics: some of the work is getting
 * more valuable and some is being absorbed by tools, and the quiz maps which
 * is which. Deliberately promises a map rather than a score, because the quiz
 * itself refuses to hand out a number, a tier or an archetype.
 *
 * Four surfaces, four registers. The banner (heading) and the sidebar carry
 * the landing page's headline verbatim: both are read at browsing pace, so the
 * exact message match is worth more than brevity. The sticky bar is on screen
 * the whole time and has one line to work with, so it drops the job title the
 * surrounding page already establishes. The slide-in arrives mid-article and
 * asks rather than announces. The shared phrase "still need a person" is what
 * keeps them matched to the landing page, so keep it if you rewrite one.
 *
 * FIRST DRAFT: the four sticky-bar/slide-in strings are AI-drafted placeholders
 * awaiting Mark's rewrite. Everything else is his.
 */
export const CTA_PRIMARY: CTAContent = {
  heading: 'Which parts of the Scrum Master job still need a person?',
  subHeading: 'Eight questions, about three minutes. No score, no archetype.',
  stickyBarText: 'Which parts of your job still need a person?',
  stickyBarButtonText: 'Show me the map',
  slideInHeading: 'Which parts of your job could a tool already do?',
  slideInBody: 'Eight questions, about three minutes.',
  slideInButtonPrimaryText: 'I’m not sure',
  slideInButtonSecondaryText: 'I think I know',
  sidebarBody:
    'Eight questions. Three minutes. See which parts of the work are getting more valuable, and which parts the tools are starting to do. No score, no archetype, just what I see and where I’d start.',
  sidebarButtonText: 'Take the Quiz',
  bodyText:
    'Some of the Scrum Master job is getting more valuable, and some of it is quietly being absorbed by tools. Answer eight questions about how you actually spent your last couple of Sprints, and you’ll get a map of which is which, plus the one change I’d make first.',
  buttonText: 'Show Me the Map',
  buttonLink: '/quiz/scrum-master-ai/',
};

/**
 * Variant B content for A/B testing
 * Set to null when no A/B test is running; populate with CTAContent to activate.
 *
 * No test is running. The previous test (AI-failure quiz vs. direct download of
 * the "20 Failure Modes" guide) retired with the AI-failure quiz. The new quiz
 * has no matching lead magnet, and splitting traffic before it has a baseline
 * conversion number would only produce two half-sized samples, so everyone sees
 * CTA_PRIMARY until there is a real hypothesis to test.
 */
export const CTA_VARIANT: CTAContent | null = null;

/**
 * Combined variants map for easy lookup by ID
 */
const variantEntry: Record<string, CTAContent> = CTA_VARIANT
  ? { [CTA_VARIANT_IDS.variant]: CTA_VARIANT }
  : {};

export const CTA_VARIANTS: Record<string, CTAContent> = {
  [CTA_VARIANT_IDS.primary]: CTA_PRIMARY,
  ...variantEntry,
};

/**
 * Default text content for CTA components (backward compatibility)
 */
export const CTA_DEFAULTS = {
  ...CTA_PRIMARY,
  postHogButtonID: 'cta-button-click-posthog',
} as const;

/**
 * Shared images for CTA components
 *
 * Both images are left over from the AI-failure-modes campaign and are about
 * GenAI coding, not the Scrum Master role. They still read as "AI", but a
 * cover that matches the role quiz would suit the copy better. The pinned
 * surfaces carry no image at all: a bottom-corner card has no room for one.
 */
export const BANNER_IMAGES: {
  image: ImageMetadata;
} = {
  image: BannerImage,
};

/**
 * Sidebar image. Carries its own imageAlt because the sidebar has no behaviour
 * config to hang it off. Imported separately from BANNER_IMAGES so the two
 * surfaces can diverge without one silently changing the other.
 */
export const SIDEBAR_IMAGES: {
  image: ImageMetadata;
  imageAlt: string;
} = {
  image: SidebarImage,
  imageAlt: 'sketch of GenAI promises vs reality',
};

/**
 * Slide-in behaviour.
 *
 * The suppression clock starts when the slide-in APPEARS, not when it is
 * dismissed, which is what the retired modal did too. Keeping that unchanged is
 * what makes the launch numbers comparable to the modal's: only the surface
 * changed, not how often it is allowed to show.
 */
export const SLIDE_IN_CONFIG = {
  /** Share of the page scrolled before it appears, 0..1 of full scroll depth. */
  scrollTriggerFraction: 0.5,
  displayIntervalDays: 15,
  /**
   * Names the panel for screen readers. Generic on purpose: CTA_PRIMARY has
   * pointed at an ebook before and will point at something else again, and a
   * landmark label that says "quiz" would then be a lie.
   */
  ariaLabel: 'Newsletter and quiz invitation',
} as const;

/**
 * Shared by both pinned surfaces, which have one dismiss control each and no
 * reason to word it differently. The sticky bar needs no config of its own:
 * its behaviour (dismissable, session-scoped) is entirely in storage.ts.
 */
export const CTA_DISMISS_LABEL = 'Dismiss';

/**
 * Content pages (those behind src/pages/[id].astro) show the sticky bar by
 * default. It is withheld from any page marked `noIndex` in frontmatter, since
 * every one of those is mid-flow for something else, plus the slugs below.
 *
 * Deliberately NOT derived from `noIndex` alone: "don't index this" and "don't
 * advertise on this" are two different intentions that merely overlap, and
 * these two pages are where they come apart.
 */
export const STICKY_BAR_EXCLUDED_PAGES: readonly string[] = [
  'privacy-policy',
  // Someone here is mid-action on something worth more than a quiz.
  'contact-us',
];

/**
 * Type for attribution sources
 */
export type Attribution =
  | 'glossary'
  | 'blog'
  | 'home-page'
  /** Any content page behind src/pages/[id].astro. */
  | 'page'
  /** The /learn page, which names itself rather than using 'page'. */
  | 'learn-resources-page';

</context>

<context ref="file:///Users/marklevison/Documents/GitHub/APR/agile-pain-relief-astro/src/lib/newsletter-tags.ts">
import { SignupType, SignupSource } from '@/constants/signup';

/**
 * Destination forms (the AI lead-magnet pages) sit on a page that isn't itself
 * the signup origin — the user clicked a CTA elsewhere to get here. That origin
 * rides along in the link's UTM params (set by `addUTMParams`: `utm_source` =
 * page attribution, `utm_medium` = the CTA surface). These map the params back
 * to the tag enums so the origin is preserved instead of being flattened to the
 * destination page. Absent/unknown values fall back.
 *
 * `'popup'` is still read even though no surface emits it any more: links built
 * before the modal was retired are still out there in inboxes and bookmarks.
 * `'sticky-bar'` and `'slide-in'` are deliberately NOT mapped — they only ever
 * link to the quiz, never to a destination form, so a case for them would be a
 * tag nothing could produce.
 */
export function sourceFromUtm(utmSource: string | null): SignupSource {
  switch (utmSource) {
    case 'home-page':
      return SignupSource.Homepage;
    case 'blog':
      return SignupSource.Blog;
    case 'glossary':
      return SignupSource.Glossary;
    default:
      return SignupSource.Other;
  }
}

export function typeFromUtm(
  utmMedium: string | null,
  fallback: SignupType
): SignupType {
  switch (utmMedium) {
    case 'inline':
      return SignupType.Inline;
    case 'popup':
      return SignupType.Popup;
    default:
      return fallback;
  }
}

/**
 * Append the type + source tags (plus any extra raw tags, e.g. `aiquiz`) to a
 * Cakemail form submission as `tags[<name>]=true`. The `SignupType`/`SignupSource`
 * enum values ARE the tag names, so they go straight onto the form. See
 * `src/constants/signup.ts` for the taxonomy.
 */
export function appendSignupTags(
  formData: FormData,
  options: {
    type: SignupType;
    source: SignupSource;
    extraTags?: readonly string[];
  }
): void {
  for (const tag of [
    options.type,
    options.source,
    ...(options.extraTags ?? []),
  ]) {
    formData.append(`tags[${tag}]`, 'true');
  }
}

</context>

<context ref="file:///Users/marklevison/Documents/GitHub/APR/agile-pain-relief-astro/src/pages/[id].astro#L76:81">
// Content pages carry the sticky bar by default. A `noIndex` page is always
// mid-flow for something else (thank-you, confirmation, pre-course prep), and
// the named exclusions are pages where a quiz invite is noise. See
// STICKY_BAR_EXCLUDED_PAGES for why the two rules are kept separate.
const showStickyBar =
  !(page.data.noIndex ?? false) && !STICKY_BAR_EXCLUDED_PAGES.includes(page.id);

</context>

/**
 * Tag taxonomy for browser-direct Cakemail newsletter signups.
 *
 * Every signup carries two tags, applied together in the one form POST:
 *   - TYPE   (which widget the person used)
 *   - SOURCE (which page they were on)
 *
 * Each enum member's VALUE is the literal Cakemail tag, so the call site reads
 * clearly (`SignupType.Popup`) while the wire value is the tag itself — no
 * separate lookup table. Names match tags already in the Cakemail account
 * (except `SignupSidebar`, which auto-creates on first use). Cakemail lowercases
 * every tag on storage, so segment queries use the lowercased form
 * (`signuppopup`, `fromhomepage`, …). See [[reference-cakemail-lowercase-tags]].
 *
 * The hosted form REPLACES a contact's whole tag set on each submission, so
 * these are additive only WITHIN a single submission — a later signup on a
 * different form overwrites them. That's accepted: the same person signing up
 * twice via different widgets is rare. See [[reference-cakemail-form-replaces-tags]].
 */

/** TYPE axis: the widget the person submitted. */
export enum SignupType {
  Inline = 'SignupNewsletterForm',
  Sidebar = 'SignupSidebar',
  Webinar = 'SignupWebinar',
  Banner = 'SignupBanner',
  Popup = 'SignupPopup',
}

/** SOURCE axis: the page the signup happened on. Coarse by design — anything that isn't homepage/blog/glossary is `Other`. */
export enum SignupSource {
  Homepage = 'FromHomepage',
  Blog = 'FromBlog',
  Glossary = 'FromGlossary',
  Other = 'FromOther',
}

**`cta.ts` — 200 → 144 lines**, almost all of it comment. `STICKY_BAR_EXCLUDED_PAGES` is now private and wrapped in `showStickyBarOn(page)`, so `[id].astro` is one call and the policy lives in one place.

## The source question

Passing `SignupSource` into `CtaStickyBar` as a prop wouldn't have done anything — the bar renders a link, not a form, so there's nothing for a signup tag to attach to. The origin was already travelling, on the link's `utm_source`/`utm_medium`. What was missing was at the far end: the quiz never read them.

So I wired the actual thing. `GatedQuizStepper` now reads the UTM params off the landing URL and appends the `SignupSource`/`SignupType` tags, exactly as the AI lead-magnet forms already do. `SignupType` gained `StickyBar` and `SlideIn` (both auto-create in Cakemail on first submission). A quiz signup now records which surface produced it instead of only recording that it came from the quiz.

## "Show me the map"

You're right — the sticky bar has no body copy, so "map" arrives unexplained. I've set it to **"Find out"**, which answers the question the bar asks. Alternatives:

| Option | Why |
|---|---|
| **Find out** (current) | Shortest, and grammatically answers "Which parts…?" |
| **Take the quiz** | Sets the expectation honestly; "quiz" is a low-threat word |
| **8 questions, 3 minutes** | States the cost instead of commanding; no verb, high trust |
| **See which** | Echoes the question's own wording |

I left `buttonText: 'Show Me the Map'` on the banner alone — its `bodyText` says "you'll get a map of which is which", so there the phrase is earned.

lastPrompt: Add a task to OmniFocus for Sept 21 to evaluate the experimental data on the success of the StickyBar/SlideIn.

content.text: **Marketing Experiments** (`APR Business Owner`) is the right home — its note says "One task per experiment."

tasks.task_name: Evaluate sticky bar / slide-in vs. the old modal popup
tasks.note:
Experiment: on 2026-08-06 the blocking modal popup was replaced by two non-blocking CTA surfaces. Sticky bar (bottom edge) on home, blog/glossary index pages, blog categories and most content pages. Slide-in (50% scroll, dismissable, 15-day suppression) on blog posts and glossary entries. Both link to /quiz/scrum-master-ai/. Nothing asks for an email; the quiz's own capture step still does.

WHERE THE DATA IS (PostHog):
- cta_shown / cta_dismissed, properties { surface, attribution, path }. surface is 'sticky-bar' or 'slide-in'.
- Clicks: autocapture, on the data-ph-capture-attribute-cta-surface attribute.
- quiz_started, property { quiz }.
- utm_medium on the landing URL is 'sticky-bar' or 'slide-in'. The slide-in's two buttons differ only by utm_content ('not-sure' vs 'i-think-i-know') - that is the framing test.
- Quiz signups now carry SignupStickyBar / SignupSlideIn plus a From* source tag in Cakemail (lowercased on storage).

THE QUESTION: which surface produces FINISHERS, not just clickers. The honest chain is cta_shown -> click -> quiz_started -> quiz completion -> opt-in. A surface with a high CTR and no completions is worse than the reverse.

COMPARISON BASELINE: the modal used the same 15-day suppression and the same clock (timed from appearance, not dismissal), so the slide-in's numbers are comparable to it. The sticky bar has no predecessor.

WATCH FOR: sticky bar dismiss rate. It is session-scoped and cannot be re-shown after a dismissal, so a high rate means it is annoying rather than merely ignored. Also whether the slide-in's two framings differ at all - if not, collapse to one button.

IF IT IS WORKING: the obvious next test is CTA_VARIANT (currently null, AB_TEST_ENABLED false). The shelved idea worth revisiting is prefill - putting the quiz's profile question in the slide-in and carrying the answer through. See HISTORY.md 2026-08-06 for why it was deferred.

Copy in src/constants/cta.ts is a first draft awaiting a rewrite - check it was actually rewritten before drawing conclusions about the copy.
